messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Spironolactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic.
Spironolactone is used for heart failure.
Spironolactone is used for high blood pressure.
Spironolactone is used for fluid build-up caused by liver or kidney disease.
Spironolactone is used for a hormone condition called primary hyperaldosteronism.
Spironolactone is sometimes prescribed off-label for women with acne or excessive facial hair growth (hirsutism).
Spironolactone works by blocking a hormone called aldosterone.
Aldosterone causes your body to pass more salt and water in your urine.
Aldosterone keeps potassium in.
Spironolactone is called potassium-sparing.
Spironolactone makes spironolactone different from most other water pills.
Most other water pills flush potassium out.
Spironolactone blocks androgens such as testosterone from binding to the androgen receptor.
This mechanism explains several of Spironolactone's side effects.
These side effects include breast tenderness and breast growth.
Spironolactone is FDA-approved to treat adults with:
Triples: [["Spironolactone", "has drug class", "potassium-sparing diuretic"], ["Spironolactone", "treats", "heart failure"], ["Spironolactone", "treats", "high blood pressure"], ["Spironolactone", "treats", "fluid build-up caused by liver or kidney disease"], ["Spironolactone", "treats", "primary hyperaldosteronism"], ["Spironolactone", "used off label in", "women with acne or hirsutism"], ["Spironolactone", "has mechanism of action", "blocking aldosterone"], ["Aldosterone", "causes", "increased salt and water excretion in urine"], ["Aldosterone", "retains", "potassium"], ["Spironolactone", "has alternative name", "potassium-sparing"], ["Spironolactone", "differs from", "most other water pills"], ["Most other water pills", "cause", "potassium loss"], ["Spironolactone", "blocks", "androgens from binding to androgen receptor"], ["This mechanism", "explains", "Spironolactone's side effects"], ["Spironolactone", "has side effect", "breast tenderness"], ["Spironolactone", "has side effect", "breast growth"], ["Spironolactone", "is fda approved for", "adults with"]]
Relations: ["blocks", "cause", "causes", "differs from", "explains", "has alternative name", "has drug class", "has mechanism of action", "has side effect", "is fda approved for", "retains", "treats", "used off label in"]
Answer:

completion:
blocks: The subject entity prevents or inhibits the action of the object entity.
cause: The subject entity is responsible for or leads to the occurrence of the object entity.
causes: The subject entity is responsible for or leads to the occurrence of the object entity.
differs from: The subject entity is different or distinct from the object entity in some characteristic or function.
explains: The subject entity provides an explanation or rationale for the object entity.
has alternative name: The subject entity is also known by the alternative name specified by the object entity.
has drug class: The subject entity is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
has mechanism of action: The subject entity functions through the mechanism of action specified by the object entity.
has side effect: The subject entity may cause the adverse effect specified by the object entity.
is fda approved for: The subject entity is approved by the FDA for use in the condition or group specified by the object entity.
retains: The subject entity helps to maintain or keep the object entity within the body.
treats: The subject entity is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
used off label in: The subject entity is used in the condition or group specified by the object entity, although it is not FDA-approved for that use.
